title: Prehabilitation for children having planned lower limb surgery: can preparation before surgery improve recovery?
official: Pre-operative rehabilitation (prehabilitation) in elective lower limb paediatric orthopaedic surgery
summary:
Background and study aims
Waiting times for children needing bone and joint surgery are increasing, which can be difficult for children and their families. In adults, rehabilitation programmes before surgery (known as prehabilitation) can help improve recovery and reduce length of hospital stay, and there is some evidence to suggest it’s more cost-effective for the NHS. However, we don’t know if this works the same way for children. Before starting PREPARE KIDS, we carried out a smaller study. The results suggested that prehabilitation could reduce the time children spend in hospital after surgery. The programme involved children learning how to use walking aids, practising exercises similar to those they may do after surgery, and understanding what to expect during recovery. We are now carrying out a larger study. The aim of the PREPARE KIDS study is to find out whether this prehabilitation programme can improve recovery in children undergoing planned lower limb surgery. The main measure of recovery will be children's functional mobility at two weeks after surgery, assessed using the PROMIS questionnaire.

Who can participate?
Children aged 5 to 14 years old (i.e., from their 5th birthday up to, but not including, their 15th birthday) who are awaiting planned (non-emergency) hip, leg or foot surgery. 

What does the study involve?
Once participants agree to take part, they will complete questionnaires before surgery. Children will then be randomly assigned to one of two groups. One group will receive a prehabilitation ('Get-Ready') session alongside usual care before surgery. This session includes learning how to use mobility aids if needed, practising exercises similar to those used after surgery, and discussing what to expect during recovery. The other group will receive usual NHS care alone. Usual care refers to the standard care children normally receive before surgery. This may vary slightly between hospitals but can include discussing the procedure with doctors, a clinical examination, and any necessary tests before surgery.
The child's surgery and postoperative care will take place as planned, regardless of which group they are assigned to.
Participants will be asked to complete follow-up questionnaires 2, 6, and 12 weeks after surgery. 

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participation will help researchers understand whether preparing children for surgery can improve recovery. The findings may help improve care for children undergoing planned lower limb surgery in the future. The study team will also aim to make participation a positive experience and provide support and reassurance for children and their families throughout surgery and recovery.
Taking part in this study is considered safe; however, the following should be noted:
Exercises: Children allocated to the prehabilitation group will be asked to complete exercises before surgery. These exercises require additional time and may cause temporary muscle tiredness or mild discomfort.
Mobility aid training: Some children may receive training in the use of mobility aids, such as crutches or walking frames. As with normal use of these aids, there is a small risk of slipping or minor injury. Training will be provided by a qualified clinician to ensure safe use.

Where is the study run from?
The study is sponsored by the University of Oxford. It is coordinated and managed by the Surgical Intervention Trials Unit (SITU), part of the Oxford Clinical Trials Research Unit (OCTRU) at the University of Oxford. The study will take place at participating NHS hospitals across the United Kingdom.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
August 2026 to October 2028

Who is funding the study? 
The study is funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Health Technology Assessment (HTA) Programme (UK)

Who is the main contact?
1. Marie-Caroline Nogaro, marie-caroline.nogaro@ndorms.ox.ac.uk 
2. PREPARE KIDS team, preparekids@ndorms.ox.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Main Study: 
1. Aged 5-14 years (i.e., from their 5th birthday up to, but not including, their 15th birthday at the time of consent) 
2. Scheduled for elective lower-limb surgery (hips to toes, excluding toenail surgery)

Process Evaluation:
Children:
1. Currently enrolled in the main study
2. Parent/guardian has provided informed consent for the child’s participation in the interview study
3. Child is willing and able to participate in the interview 

Parent/Guardian:
1. Parent/Guardian of a participant enrolled in the main study
2. Has provided consent to be contacted regarding interview study 
3. Willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the interview study

Site Clinical/Research Staff: 
1. Clinical and research staff participating in the PREPARE KIDS study
2. Willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the interview study
Exclusion criteria:
Main Study: 
1. The child is currently receiving a physiotherapy programme which replicates the content of PREPARE KIDS
2. The child and/or their parent(s)/guardian(s) are unable to comply with assessment procedures
3. Previous participation in PREPARE KIDS study

Process Evaluation:
Children:
1. Withdrawn from the main study

Parent/Guardian: 
1. No longer acting as parent/guardian of a participant enrolled in the main study 
2. Child withdrawn from the main study

Site Clinical/Research Staff: 
1. No longer involved in the conduct of the main study
